transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, well, what finally pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up during important meetings when I know I really should just stay put. Like during our sprint planning at work, or... oh, especially during these mortgage calls I've been having lately. We're trying to refinance because the rates are just doing all sorts of crazy things right now, and our current broker is this guy named Dan who talks *so* slowly. Like, painfully slow. 

But anyway, I'll be on the call and I'll just suddenly decide I need to go get water, or I'll decide to go check something in the other room and just get up and walk away. Speaking of water, we just got one of those new fridge filters and the water pressure on it is terrible, it takes forever to fill a glass, which is super annoying. But yeah, I just can't seem to stay in my chair when I'm supposed to be listening.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or wired for several days in a row?

Wired for several days? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I drink a lot of coffee, especially when we're pushing a new software release at work, but not like... energized for days on end. 

Speaking of coffee, my husband actually just bought me this incredibly complicated pour-over setup for my birthday last month. It has this fancy gooseneck kettle that tells you the exact temperature of the water. He's really into all that precision stuff right now, which is so funny to me because he's an art teacher, you know? You'd think he'd be a little more... free-flowing, I guess? But he is absolutely obsessed with getting the water to exactly 205 degrees. It takes him like fifteen minutes just to make a single cup of coffee, and I just don't have the patience to stand there and watch it drip. I end up just using the Keurig anyway because I just want to grab it and get back to my desk. 

But wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the energy thing. Yeah, no, I usually crash pretty hard at night, so definitely not days in a row.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble sitting still in class?

Oh, definitely. I remember in elementary school, my teachers were always having to move my desk around or remind me to stay seated. I was just constantly popping up out of my chair. And I'd always blurt out answers before they called on me, or I'd just rush through my work even if I totally understood it. 

Actually, speaking of elementary school, my daughter is in third grade right now, and her teacher is doing this new thing where they sit on these giant yoga balls instead of chairs? Which I guess is supposed to help them focus, but honestly, it just sounds like a recipe for disaster to me. Like, I would have just been bouncing all over the classroom on one of those things. My daughter loves it, though. She says it's way better than the hard plastic chairs. We actually had to buy her one for the house because she was begging for it, but she mostly just rolls around on it while she's watching TV. 

But yeah, I was definitely one of those kids who had a really hard time just staying in my seat.
Do you often feel hard-to-control worry?

Worry? I mean, not really hard-to-control, no. I worry about normal things, like my daughter's grades or if we're going to get this refinancing done before the rates go up again. Which reminds me, Dan the broker sent over another massive stack of paperwork yesterday, and it's all digital, but they still want physical signatures on half of it. It's so frustrating because our printer has been out of cyan ink for like three weeks. Why does it even need cyan to print a black-and-white document? It just refuses to print anything at all. My husband was supposed to pick up the ink on his way home from school, but he got distracted by some gallery opening downtown. He’s been talking about submitting some of his own pieces to a gallery, actually. He does these huge, abstract canvas things. They take up half the garage right now. 

But um, worry... no, I wouldn't say I have like, uncontrollable worry. Just regular stuff.
Do you often act before thinking?

Act before thinking? Um, not really. I mean, I usually plan things out pretty well. Especially at work, you can't really just write code and send it off without thinking it through. We have this whole review process before anything goes live. 

Although, speaking of things going live, they just updated our entire project management system over the weekend, and it is a complete disaster. The interface is totally different, and all the buttons are in the wrong places now. It took me like twenty minutes just to figure out how to log my hours on Monday. And the color scheme! They changed it to this awful neon green that just completely strains my eyes. I was complaining to my husband about it, and he said I should just get those blue-light blocking glasses, which is hilarious because I actually bought a pair last year and almost immediately lost them. I'm pretty sure they fell behind the couch in the living room. We really need to pull that couch out and vacuum back there anyway. The dog's tennis balls always end up rolling underneath it, and then he just sits there and whines at the cushions until someone fishes them out with a broom handle. 

But wait, sorry, acting before thinking? Yeah, no, I wouldn't say I do that. I'm pretty careful about things.
Do you often feel restless, like you have to keep moving even when you’re supposed to stay seated?

Yeah, I actually do. It's weird because even when I’m sitting totally calmly on the outside, like in a meeting or something, I feel this huge pressure inside. Like I just desperately need to move, or switch tasks, or do something with my hands before I crawl right out of my skin. 

It happens a lot during our sprint planning meetings. Which, by the way, they just moved to Thursday afternoons, which is honestly the worst possible time. By Thursday at 3 PM, everyone is just completely checked out. And they started catering those meetings, but it's always from this one deli down the street that puts way too much mayo on literally everything. I don't know who is in charge of ordering the sandwiches—probably Greg from HR—but I swear I asked for a plain turkey wrap last time and it was just drenched. I ended up having to walk all the way down to the lobby cafe just to get a bran muffin instead. 

The barista down there, she actually just started a coding bootcamp, which is so cool. I was giving her some tips on Python last week because she was getting super stuck on building loops, and I remember when I was first learning that stuff back in college it was so frustrating. My professor for that class was this guy who mumbled so quietly you couldn't hear him past the second row... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, being restless. But yeah, I definitely get that internal crawling feeling a lot, even if I look perfectly still.
